import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 11

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/11](https://www.erdosproblems.com/11)
-/

namespace Erdos11

/--
Is every odd $n > 1$ the sum of a squarefree number and a power of 2?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_11 (n : ℕ) (hn : Odd n) (hn' : 1 < n) :
    ∃ k l : ℕ, Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2 ^ l := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős often asked this under the weaker assumption that $n > 1$
is not divisible by 4.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_11.variants.not_four_dvd (n : ℕ) (hn : ¬ 4 ∣ n) (hn' : 1 < n) :
    ∃ k l : ℕ , Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2^l := by
  sorry

/--
Is every odd $n > 1$ the sum of a squarefree number and two powers of 2?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_11.variants.two_pow_two (n : ℕ) (hn : Odd n) (hn' : 1 < n) :
    ∃ k l m : ℕ , Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2^l + 2^m := by
  sorry

/--
Every odd $1 < n < 10^7$ is the sum of a squarefree number and a power of 2.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_11.variants.finite_bound1 (n : ℕ) (hn : Odd n) (h : n < 10^7) (hn' : 1 < n) :
    ∃ k l : ℕ , Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2^l := by
  sorry

/--
Every odd $1 < n < 2^50$ is the sum of a squarefree number and a power of 2.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_11.variants.finite_bound2 (n : ℕ) (hn : Odd n) (h : n < 2^50) (hn' : 1 < n) :
    ∃ k l : ℕ , Squarefree k ∧ n = k + 2^l := by
  sorry

/--
Suppose that every odd $n$ is the sum of a squarefree number and a power of 2. Then the set of primes
$p$ such that $2 ^ p ≡ 2 \mod p ^ 2$ is infinite. This is Theorem 1 in [GrSo98].
[GrSo98] Granville, A. and Soundararajan, K., A Binary Additive Problem of Erdős and the Order of $2$ mod $p^2$. The Ramanujan Journal (1998), 283-298.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_11.variants.granville_soundararajan (H : type_of% erdos_11) :
    {p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ 2 ^ p ≡ 2 [MOD p ^ 2]}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos11

findings.description: The conclusion at line 75 selects Wieferich primes, but the cited theorem concerns non-Wieferich primes. For prime p, `2 ^ p ≡ 2 [MOD p ^ 2]` is equivalent to `2 ^ (p - 1) ≡ 1 [MOD p ^ 2]`; this equivalence, including p = 2, was proved independently in the scratch file. Thus the missing negation changes which class of primes is asserted to be infinite. It is not an exponent reindexing or a status issue. The docstring repeats the same mathematical error.
findings.source_evidence: Granville and Soundararajan, A Binary Additive Problem of Erdős and the Order of 2 mod p², The Ramanujan Journal 2 (1998), Theorem 1, p. 284: under the representation conjecture, “there are infinitely many primes p for which p² does not divide 2^(p−1) − 1.” Read in the publisher's two-page preview: https://page-one.springer.com/pdf/preview/10.1007/978-1-4757-4507-8_17 . The current https://www.erdosproblems.com/11 likewise explicitly says “non-Wieferich primes.”
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the conclusion with `{p : ℕ | p.Prime ∧ ¬ (2 ^ p ≡ 2 [MOD p ^ 2])}.Infinite`, retaining the existing hypothesis H. Update the docstring to say that the congruence does not hold.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses `n < 10 ^ 7`, whereas the webpage describes verification “up to 10^7,” which can be read inclusively.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The endpoint 10^7 is even, so an odd n cannot equal it. Under the common hypotheses Odd n and 1 < n, the strict and inclusive bounds therefore give identical domains. The equivalence of the complete universally quantified theorem types was proved in /workspace/review/boundaries.lean.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses `n < 2 ^ 50`, while the webpage says “up to 2^50.” Hercher's detailed theorem itself uses the strict bound.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Since 2^50 is even, Odd n implies n ≠ 2^50. Consequently n < 2^50 and n ≤ 2^50 are equivalent on the stated domain. The equivalence of the complete theorem types was proved in /workspace/review/boundaries.lean.

https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/11 — exact formulas and bibliography; read through https://r.jina.ai/http://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/11 .

Erdős, A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory (1980), p. 96: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-03.pdf .

Local definition sources: Mathlib.Algebra.Squarefree.Basic, Mathlib.Data.Nat.Squarefree, Mathlib.Algebra.Ring.Parity, Mathlib.Data.Nat.Prime.Defs, Mathlib.Data.Nat.ModEq, Mathlib.Data.Finite.Defs; FormalConjecturesUtil answer/category machinery; Lean.Elab.BuiltinTerm's type_of% elaborator.
could_not_verify: Erdos11.erdos_11.variants.two_pow_two: The webpage mentions the two-power variant without spelling out its lower cutoff, while its main question currently says “large” odd integers. I did not obtain a primary passage explicitly posing the two-power variant for every odd n>1, or establish equivalence with the sufficiently-large version. Its Lean predicate and small cases check out, but that exact quantifier-scope/source question remains unsettled; it is not reported as a confirmed defect.
review.notes: All six declarations and their supporting definitions were inspected. Scratch files under /workspace/review compiled successfully; checks covered Squarefree at 0 and 1, the smallest admissible n, the full expansion of type_of%, small representation searches, and prime-congruence boundary cases. The congruence identification was proved without sorry axioms. The main theorem's all-odd-n>1 version is explicitly supported by Hercher's Conjecture 1, despite the webpage's current “large” wording; the not-four-divisible version is explicitly posed by Erdős in 1985. No separate stale status record was found.

not_demonstrated.reason: No short proof or disproof of the actual conditional infinitude statement is available. Small-prime checks distinguish Wieferich from non-Wieferich primes, but do not refute either infinitude claim: both classes could be infinite. The existing predicate-equivalence proof therefore does not meet the requested exact-statement demonstration criterion.

submission.summary: The source comparison establishes the missing negation, but it does not supply a trivial proof or counterexample to the declaration as written. No trivial_proof.lean was created; its absence was checked.
submission.gave_up_reason: The reported defect switches the class of primes in a nontrivial infinitude conclusion. It produces neither a known contradictory hypothesis nor a finite counterexample to the theorem. Presenting a pointwise predicate mismatch as a disproof of the theorem would be misleading.

submission.summary: Negated the congruence so the conclusion asserts infinitude of non-Wieferich primes, as the cited theorem states. Updated the docstring accordingly and made its existing n > 1 hypothesis explicit. All other declarations and attributes are unchanged. The specified Lean compilation passed with only the existing `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
